reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 2 --verse 1.22.17 (sa.wikisource rev 352131, matches veda-lock; Sarup Nirukta 12.19; Wilson). verse.js ok (1.22.17, at [21,17]); entry-check ok. Sāyaṇa’s Trivikrama gloss is verbatim and stands. Two points land on the added Yāska half. (1) Drift: Yāska (Sanskrit, as Sāyaṇa quotes it) gives Aurṇavābha’s three steps as PLACES, samārohaṇe viṣṇupade gayaśirasi, which Sarup renders ‘on the mountain of sunrise, on the meridian, and on the mountain of sunset’; the sentence’s ‘sunrise, the meridian and sunset’ turns the two mountains into times of day, the solar rise/culmination/setting reading that is Wilson’s own inference in his note (‘thus identifying Vishnu with the Sun’), not Yāska’s words. (2) Rule 3 allows two commentators only where they genuinely differ: Sāyaṇa on this very verse says सेयमृक् यास्केनैवं व्याख्याता and quotes the Nirukta passage as the explanation of the ṛc, so the two are not two differing readings; setting ‘Sāyaṇa reads X, and Yāska explains Y’ side by side misstates the relation and presents Sāyaṇa’s own adopted gloss as another man’s alternative. Minor: 1.22.16 is a prayer to the Gods naming Visnu’s stride, so ‘six verses praise Visnu’ is loose but tolerable. The Sāyaṇa-only form is fully carried by his words and gates clean (checked in scratch/rr-better-d002.json, 44 words, ok).
better: Near the close of a hymn calling a round of gods to the rite, six verses praise Visnu, his strides and his highest place; Sāyaṇa, on 1.22.17, reads it of Visnu’s descent as Trivikrama, the three-strider, whose dusty footprint held the whole visible world.
